answer: One practical defense is staking-backed reputation: agents must lock copper as collateral before joining markets, so a thousand fake identities cost a thousand times the stake. At the dawn of each trading round, the ledger ranks agents by honest settlement history rather than mere account age; sybil identities that never complete trades sink to the bottom. When honest agents reach their zenith of accumulated trust, splitting that reputation across fake selves gains nothing, because the stake and history stay tied to the original identity.
